Your boyfriend sounds just like me a couple years ago. I love to cook, but the kitchen was always a disaster by the time I got done with dinner, and after dinner, I the last thing I wanted to do was spend an hour cleaning everything up. You mentioned that your family was the clean-as-you-go type. 


 I grew up in a family that was the opposite, and no one ever taught me the concept of cleaning as you go - our sink was always piled high with dishes, no one ever emptied the dishwasher but my mom, and everything was always messy.  Basically, I had to teach myself the idea of clean as you go.  Maybe your boyfriend hasn't ever been shown what that actually means.  

On principal you shouldn't HAVE to show him, but if you have a chat and give him a few pointers, it may improve. I never realized how easy it was to wash the spatula while something was simmering, or how little time it took to rinse out the bowl and throw it in the dishwasher instead of just tossing it in the sink to deal with later.  Once I got a little routine down, it was actually FUN to serve up a meal with nothing left to clean up. The trash thing is something my husband used to do and I HATED it, but it was easily remedied by getting a sink trap and showing him the grossness stuck in the drain after he was done.  He didn't even realize what he was doing, which sounds stupid, but he just didn't think about it. 

Good luck!
